chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Zurara from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)

Regarding a man who transfers the debt of another man to a third party, and the original debtor says to the new debtor: 'You are free from my debt to you.' He (the Imam) said: 'If he discharges him (grants him freedom from the debt), then he has no right to return to him; and if he does not discharge him, then he has the right to return to the one who transferred the debt to him.'
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurara

key_terms.أَبْرَأَهُ: He discharged him (granted freedom from obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect of discharging a new debtor in a debt transfer (hiwalah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the conditions of *hiwalah* (debt transfer) through the chain of prominent narrators like Zurarah, highlighting the critical distinction between a simple transfer and a full discharge (*ibra*). It establishes that the original debtor's right to recourse against the new debtor is contingent upon whether an explicit release was granted, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the clarity of contractual intent in financial transactions.
